entries.summary: Ten Western hands link particular Dragons with specific suits or coloured rank groups.
entries.whatItIs: These are separate named hands. The useful clue is the Dragon colour and the restricted suited tiles used with it.
entries.whatItMeans: Choose a hand below to see its exact Dragon and suit rule.
entries.whySpecial: The names are easier to understand when the colour patterns are shown together.

variants.label: Blue Mountains
variants.definition: Green Dragon Pung with three Pungs/Kongs and a pair from the blue Circle ranks 2,3,4,5,8,9.

variants.label: White Elephant
variants.definition: White Dragon Pung/Kong with even Circle Pungs/Kongs and pair.

variants.label: Driven Snow
variants.definition: White Dragon Pung with odd Character Pungs/Kongs and pair.

variants.label: Dragon's Scales
variants.definition: Red Dragon Pung with even Character Pungs/Kongs and pair.

variants.label: Lily of the Valley
variants.definition: Green and White Dragon Pungs/Kongs with green Bamboo Pungs/Kongs and pair.

variants.label: Red Waratah
variants.definition: Red Dragon Pung, one Pung in each suit with the Bamboo rank from the red Bamboo set, and a Green Dragon pair.

variants.label: Royal Ruby
variants.definition: Red Dragon Pung/Kong with red Bamboo-rank Pungs/Kongs and pair; red Bamboo ranks are 1,5,7,9.

variants.label: Red Lily
variants.definition: Red and White Dragon Pungs/Kongs with red Bamboo Pungs/Kongs and pair.

variants.label: Ruby Jade
variants.definition: Red and Green Dragon Pungs or Kongs, Bamboo Pungs or Kongs, and a pair. These rules do not restrict which Bamboo ranks go with each Dragon.

variants.label: Lillypilly
variants.definition: Green Dragon Pung, White Dragon pair, and three Circle Pungs/Kongs.

evidenceBindings.locator: Pass 4D — Blue Mountains, White Elephant, Driven Snow, Dragon's Scales, Lily of the Valley, Red Waratah, Royal Ruby, Red Lily, Ruby Jade

entries.summary: Three suited Pungs or Kongs plus all four Winds, with one Wind paired. The named hands fix or free the suited ranks.
entries.whatItIs: All three hands make one Pung or Kong in each suit, then use all four Winds with one Wind paired. Windvane allows different suited numbers; Three Sisters uses 3s; Seven Brothers uses 7s.
entries.whatItMeans: Windvane allows independent suited meld ranks; Three Sisters fixes all three melds to rank 3; Seven Brothers fixes them to rank 7.
entries.whySpecial: The suited ranks distinguish these three hands.

variants.label: Windvane
variants.definition: One Pung/Kong in each suit plus all four Winds with one Wind paired.

variants.label: Three Sisters
variants.definition: A Pung/Kong of 3s in each suit plus all four Winds with one paired.

variants.label: Seven Brothers
variants.definition: A Pung/Kong of 7s in each suit plus all four Winds with one paired.

evidenceBindings.locator: Pass 4F Wind-family hybrid wave — Windvane p.28; Three Sisters p.29; Seven Brothers p.29

entries.summary: Red and White Dragon Pungs plus a seven-tile 1-7 or 2-8 run in Characters or Circles, with one run tile paired.
entries.whatItIs: Make Red and White Dragon Pungs. Add a seven-tile 1-7 or 2-8 run in Characters or Circles, with one run tile duplicated as the pair.
entries.whatItMeans: The suited section contains every rank in a seven-tile run plus one duplicate to make its pair; the two represented Dragon groups are specifically Red and White Pungs.
entries.whySpecial: It joins two Dragon Pungs to a run with one tile paired.

evidenceBindings.locator: Pass 4G — Dragon's Teeth pp.12,33 / synopsis pp.56,58

entries.summary: Four Chows spanning all three suits plus a pair of the player's own Wind.
entries.whatItIs: Make four Chows using all three suits, then pair your seat Wind.
entries.whatItMeans: All three suits must appear among the Chows, and player context determines whether the Wind pair qualifies.
entries.whySpecial: Your seat Wind must make the pair.

evidenceBindings.locator: Pass 4G / Pass 4J — Little Brother p.17 / synopsis p.56

entries.summary: Take 1 to 7 in exactly two suits. Every tile is a single; there are no normal sets or pair.
entries.whatItIs: Use 1 to 7 once in each of exactly two suits.
entries.whatItMeans: There are no normal melds or pair; each chosen suit contributes the seven single tiles 1 through 7.
entries.whySpecial: The hand is two matching runs of single tiles, with no sets or pair.

entries.summary: Two non-terminal ranks repeated as Pungs/Kongs in each of two suits, plus an honour pair.
entries.whatItIs: Choose two non-terminal numbers and two suits. Make each number as a Pung or Kong in both suits, then add an honour pair.
entries.whatItMeans: Choose two non-terminal ranks and two suits; each rank appears as a Pung/Kong in both suits, giving four melds, then add an honour pair.
entries.whySpecial: The two numbers repeat across both suits.

entries.summary: North and South Wind Pungs or Kongs, plus 1-8-6-1 in one suit and 1-8-6-5 in another.
entries.whatItIs: Make North and South Wind Pungs or Kongs. Add 1-8-6-1 in one suit and 1-8-6-5 in another.
entries.whatItMeans: The grouped part is North and South; the remaining eight tiles form 1-8-6-1 in one suit and 1-8-6-5 in another.
entries.whySpecial: The hand uses these exact number patterns.

entries.summary: A 1-7 run with one run tile paired, plus Red Dragon and own-Wind Pungs/Kongs.
entries.whatItIs: Take 1 to 7 in one suit with one run tile duplicated. Add a Red Dragon Pung or Kong and a Pung or Kong of your seat Wind.
entries.whatItMeans: Player context matters: the Wind meld must be the player's own Wind, while the suited loose section contains 1 through 7 and one duplicate.
entries.whySpecial: The run-and-pair pattern combines a Red Dragon set with your seat Wind set.

entries.summary: Four Western hands use Mixed Chows: three consecutive numbers, one tile from each suit.
entries.whatItIs: A Mixed Chow has one Bamboo, one Circle and one Character tile whose numbers run in order, such as 1 Bamboo, 2 Circles, 3 Characters.
entries.whatItMeans: The four named hands differ in how many Mixed Chows they use and what other tiles complete the hand.
entries.whySpecial: Mixed Chows do not follow the normal same-suit Chow rule.

variants.label: Three Philosophers
variants.definition: One ordinary Chow in each suit, one Mixed Chow and a suited pair.

variants.label: Crazy Chows
variants.definition: Four Mixed Chows plus a Mixed Pair.

variants.label: Apple Blossom
variants.definition: Concealed White Dragon Pung/Kong, Green Dragon pair and three Mixed Chows.

variants.label: The Professors
variants.definition: Three Mixed Chows, one of each Dragon and the player's own-Wind pair.

evidenceBindings.locator: Pass 4K Mixed Chow family — Three Philosophers p.15/p.56; Crazy Chows p.16/p.56; Apple Blossom p.19/pp.56,58; The Professors p.19/p.56

entries.summary: Four concealed Chows and a pair in one suit, won from the wall.
entries.whatItIs: All four sets are concealed Chows in one suit.
entries.whatItMeans: The hand must stay concealed and the winning tile must come from the wall under this rule.
entries.whySpecial: Both the all-Chow shape and how the winning tile is drawn matter.

evidenceBindings.locator: Pass 4L — Chow Chow detail p.15; synopsis pp.56,59

entries.displayName: Up You Go / Down You Go
entries.summary: All four Winds plus 2, 4, 6 and 8 in one suit, with the tile counts rising or falling.
entries.whatItIs: Up You Go uses 2, 44, 666, 8888. Down You Go reverses it: 2222, 444, 66, 8. Both also use one of each Wind.
entries.whatItMeans: Up You Go increases the count as the even rank rises: 2, 44, 666, 8888. Down You Go reverses it: 2222, 444, 66, 8. Both also contain one of each Wind.
entries.whySpecial: The two hands are mirror images, so learning them together is easier.

variants.label: Up You Go
variants.definition: ESWN plus one 2, two 4s, three 6s and four 8s in one suit.

variants.label: Down You Go
variants.definition: ESWN plus four 2s, three 4s, two 6s and one 8 in one suit.

evidenceBindings.locator: Pass 4L — Up You Go / Down You Go, Full Synopsis p.57

facetDefinitionAdditions.mixed-chow: A three-tile group with one tile from each suit whose ranks form one consecutive three-rank run; unlike an ordinary Chow, the tiles do not share a suit.
